about.title: About 24×7 ON Court
about.description: Why the 24×7 ON Court in Kollam exists, the principles behind it, who it serves, its current jurisdiction, and the people who run it.
about.heading: A court built around people’s lives.
about.intro: The idea is simple: court services should come closer to people, with clearer information, easier steps, and help when it is needed.
about.launch: The High Court of Kerala launched the first 24×7 ON Court in Kollam in November 2024, beginning with cheque dishonour cases.
about.glance.label: ON Court at a glance
about.glance.launch.caption: The first 24×7 ON Court launched in Kollam.
about.glance.access.caption: Digital services designed around people’s time and circumstances.
about.glance.stations.caption: The court’s currently listed jurisdiction within Kollam district.
about.vision.heading: Taking the court closer to the people it serves.
about.vision.body1: ON Courts is shaped by a future where courts can deliver timely services around people’s needs, location, and circumstances. Its first focus is cheque dishonour cases, using simpler processes, open information, and easier communication.
about.vision.body2: The approach supports the direction set out in Phase III of India’s e-Courts Project: make the justice journey easier to understand and act on, from filing through resolution.
about.video.heading: Meet the 24×7 ON Court in Kollam.
about.video.caption: Watch the official introduction on YouTube
about.principles.heading: The ideas behind the service.
about.principles.intro: These principles shape how information, court processes, and support are brought together.
about.principles.people.heading: People-centred
about.principles.people.body: Start with what people need. Make each step more predictable and efficient, and keep improving through user feedback.
about.principles.open.heading: Open
about.principles.open.body: Make court information useful and actionable while respecting privacy and security. Build with open technology where possible.
about.principles.networked.heading: Networked
about.principles.networked.body: Connect with allied institutions so information can move more smoothly across the justice ecosystem.
about.experience.heading: Less uncertainty. Fewer unnecessary steps.
about.experience.intro: The service aims to make case progress clearer and routine actions easier to complete.
about.experience.accessible.heading: Accessible and predictable
about.experience.accessible.body: File a case, respond to a summons, submit applications, and manage hearing dates from wherever you are. See what happens next.
about.experience.assisted.heading: Assisted and empowering
about.experience.assisted.body: Follow case updates, hearing dates, summons status, and orders. Receive prompts when action is needed.
about.experience.seamless.heading: Seamless and direct
about.experience.seamless.body: Reduce trips and repeated paperwork when signing documents, making payments, correcting errors, or tracking notices.
about.benefits.heading: A better working experience across the court.
about.benefits.intro: The same connected service supports people bringing cases and the professionals who help resolve them.
about.benefits.litigants.heading: Litigants
about.benefits.litigants.1: Receive alerts about case status and next actions.
about.benefits.litigants.2: Access case files and track progress through a personal login.
about.benefits.litigants.3: Sign documents without extra visits to an advocate.
about.benefits.advocates.heading: Advocates
about.benefits.advocates.1: File cases remotely through a guided digital process.
about.benefits.advocates.2: Get updates when a case needs attention.
about.benefits.judges.heading: Judges
about.benefits.judges.1: Access the case information needed for decisions.
about.benefits.judges.3: Sign orders digitally, including in bulk.
about.benefits.staff.heading: Court staff
about.benefits.staff.1: Review filings remotely with system support.
about.benefits.staff.2: Generate, track, and deliver processes across channels.
about.jurisdiction.heading: Starting in Kollam.
about.jurisdiction.body: The 24×7 ON Court currently accepts cheque dishonour cases under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, arising from nine police station areas in Kollam district.
about.jurisdiction.countLabel: police station areas currently mapped to the Kollam ON Court
about.jurisdiction.mapTitle: Police Stations mapped to ON Court
about.jurisdiction.mapCaption: Kollam district, with the police stations mapped to the ON Court. District outline from OpenStreetMap contributors.
about.jurisdiction.hint: Choose a police station to highlight it. Kollam West and the ON Court sit together at the district court complex.
about.quote.cite: Karthika S., Advocate · Featured on the official ON Courts site. She also suggested a chatbot to help users.

about.people.intro: Court leadership and the judicial officers serving the Kollam ON Court, brought into the same story as the service they support.

dashboard.about.title: About the figures
dashboard.about.intro: These figures were observed on the official public dashboard on {date}. This page shows a fixed snapshot and does not refresh automatically.
dashboard.about.totals.heading: Totals and quarterly activity
dashboard.about.totals.body: Filed, pending and disposed are separate source measures. The status counts are not a complete, reconciled breakdown of all filings. The quarterly disposal series shows {series} cases; the headline total is {headline}. The source does not explain the difference, and it gives no disposal figure for {missing}.
dashboard.about.stages.heading: Stages and outcomes
dashboard.about.stages.body: Stage shares divide each count by all {pending} pending cases. Outcome shares are rounded by the source and total {outcomeTotal}%. Contested rulings cover {rulings} cases: {acquitted} acquittals and {convicted} convictions.
dashboard.about.timing.heading: Time and hearings
dashboard.about.timing.body: Stage figures are medians for cases that completed that stage. They do not measure how long pending cases have been waiting. The overall figures keep the source’s labels; the source does not state how they are calculated. None of these is an estimate for an individual case.
